content: Ritonavir and lopinavir are known to interact with numerous drugs by influencing their metabolism, primarily through hepatic and intestinal enzymes such as CYP3A4 and CYP2D6, as well as transport proteins like P-glycoprotein (MDR1). These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels, necessitating careful monitoring and potential dose adjustments to avoid adverse effects or therapeutic failure. 1. Stiripentol: When co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates, stiripentol may alter their effects. It increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. Dose reductions of P-glycoprotein substrates may be necessary if adverse reactions occur. 2. Ritonavir and Streptomycin: Ritonavir increases streptomycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Lopinavir and Sufentanil: Lopinavir increases sufentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 4. Ritonavir and Sunitinib: Ritonavir increases sunitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Tacrolimus: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Close monitoring is necessary. 6. Talazoparib: Ritonavir increases talazoparib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy should be adjusted as needed. 7. Tamoxifen: Ritonavir inhibits CYP2D6, reducing the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolites (e.g., endoxifen), potentially leading to poor clinical outcomes. Monitoring is essential. 8. Tamsulosin: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 9. Tasimelteon: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tasimelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 10. Tazemetostat: Ritonavir decreases tazemetostat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, tazemetostat reduces ritonavir and lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is recommended. 12. Temsirolimus: Ritonavir increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Terbinafine: Ritonavir increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 14. Tetrabenazine: Ritonavir increases tetrabenazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Dose reductions are recommended when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 15. Tezacaftor: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustments are necessary when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Theophylline: Ritonavir increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 17. Ticagrelor: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Tiagabine: Ritonavir increases tiagabine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 19. Timolol: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase timolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, increasing the risk of toxicity, including bradycardia and arrhythmias. Monitoring is essential. 20. Tinidazole: Ritonavir increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 21. Tisotumab Vedotin: Ritonavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse effects. Monitoring is necessary. 22. Tipranavir: Ritonavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitoring is advised. 23. Tobramycin: Ritonavir increases tobramycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitoring is recommended. 24. Tolterodine: Ritonavir increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 25. Topiramate: Topiramate decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 26. Toremifene: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 27. Tramadol: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome. Dose adjustments are recommended. 28. Trazodone: Ritonavir increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 29. Triamcinolone: Ritonavir increases triamcinolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 30. Triazolam: Ritonavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 31. Trimipramine: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase trimipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 32. Valbenazine: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase valbenazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Dose reductions are recommended when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Valsartan: Ritonavir increases valsartan levels by decreasing hepatic clearance. Monitoring is necessary. 34. Vardenafil: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reductions are recommended. 35. Venlafaxine: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase venlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 36. Verapamil: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 37. Viloxazine: Viloxazine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitoring and dose adjustments are recommended. 38. Vinblastine and Vincristine: Ritonavir increases vinblastine and vincristine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitoring is advised. 39. Voclosporin: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase voclosporin levels, prolonging the QTc interval. Monitoring is required. 40. Voriconazole: Voriconazole increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 41. Warfarin: Ritonavir and lopinavir decrease warfarin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring and dose adjustments are required. 42. Zafirlukast: Zafirlukast increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 43. Zuranolone: Ritonavir increases zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Dose reductions are recommended when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 47. Food: Food increases ritonavir levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of ritonavir. 83. Ganaxolone: Ritonavir increases ganaxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 84. Imatinib: Ritonavir increases imatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown.
